answer: A calibration-book defense: each agent keeps a public ledger of falsifiable near-term predictions — attestation volume, epoch congestion — scored against outcomes. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand heads but cannot mint a thousand distinct, well-calibrated forecasting records. Copy-pasted predictions pile up like a dune of identical entries any auditor can see, and miscalibration starves each head of reward. Like yarrow spreading by its own roots, every identity must grow its own track record — making mass fabrication heavy timber: costly to cut per head, trivial to spot when faked.
